sections.body: COOKING a simple meal: plan, wash hands, prepare ingredients, cook carefully (ask an adult the first times), and clean as you go.
FOOD SAFETY: keep raw meat separate from ready-to-eat food, cook food all the way through, and refrigerate leftovers quickly.
TIME MANAGEMENT: break big tasks into smaller ones, do the hardest task when you have most energy, and use a planner.
SIMPLE FIXES: sewing a button, changing a light bulb (power off!), pumping up a bike tyre. Watch a reliable how-to with an adult.

quiz.q: Why keep raw meat separate from salad?
hints: Salad isn't cooked, so germs wouldn't be killed.
We wash hands after touching raw chicken for the same reason.
quiz.explain: Raw meat can carry bacteria. Salad isn't cooked, so keeping them apart prevents food poisoning.

quiz.q: Before changing a light bulb, you should…
hints: You unplug a toaster before getting stuck toast out. Light bulbs are similar.
quiz.explain: Always switch the power off first.

quiz.q: You have a big project due in two weeks. Which plan follows the lesson's time-management tips?
options: Break it into smaller tasks, write them in a planner, and do the hardest parts when you have most energy
Wait until the night before, when the pressure will help you focus
Do only the easiest bits each day and leave the hardest part until the end
hints: Big tasks feel easier when they're…?
The lesson gives three tips: one about splitting tasks, one about timing the hard ones, and one about a tool to track them.
Training for a 5 km run, you'd plan shorter runs over several weeks instead of trying the full 5 km for the first time on race day.
quiz.explain: The lesson's tips are to break big tasks into smaller ones, tackle the hardest task when you have most energy, and use a planner.
